question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3.
solution:
The correct answer is **"Some".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To know which of the following word is the **most appropriate** to be filled in the **blank number 3**
 
• Let’s consider the usage of the words given in the options :
 
 
• ​A little: It is used to express **uncountable nouns**, very less in quantity. We can't use 'a little' in the blank because **'questions' **is a countable noun.
 
• **Any**: It is used to express numbers in indefinite pronoun.
 
 
• **Example**: *You can buy any of these pens.*
 
 
 
• **Any** is used as an adverb in the **negative, interrogative sentences.**
 
 
• **​ Example**: *We are too tired to go **any further.***
 
 
 
• **​All **is used to show the whole of something. We can't use **All **here because the quantity is not wholesome.
 
• **Some**: is used in affirmative sentences before **uncountable nouns **to denote the quantity and it is used before** plural countable nouns to denote number**. So, its usage before 'questions' is appropriate here as it is a countable noun.
 
 
• ***Example***: *She has got **some** nice presents for Christmas this year.*
 
 
 
 
 
• *​*With the given usage and example given above, we are sure that the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'Some'.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** option 4.**

**​Correct Passage:* ****I was often invited to colleges and universities **to deliver** lectures. Once, I went to a university to deliver a lecture. **After** it was over, the students gathered to ask **some** questions. Though it was getting late (4) ______ my next programme, since I love talking to(5) ______, I remained there answering their questions.*
